page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m1.large is an entry-level, shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the ecs.e server family. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 2.0 GB of memory, resulting in a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated network bandwidth baseline, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

In terms of performance, benchmark results position this instance in the lower tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance score is 1296.39, which is categorized as weak, while the multi-core score of 1720.39 falls into the poor category. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block speed of 95.86 GB/sec, but large block uncached read and write speeds drop significantly to 2.06 GB/sec and 2.04 GB/sec respectively. Passmark CPU and memory scores also rank in the bottom 10 percent, reflecting its limited processing and memory throughput capabilities.

The instance is designed for high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency, trading raw performance for lower resource allocation costs. It is best suited for lightweight, non-critical workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, low-traffic testing, or simple background tasks that do not require sustained high CPU or memory throughput.
